messages:
saurabh (People Ops): Heads-up  we're switching our 401(k) vendor from Principal to Fidelity on 2026-07-15. Employees already asked about mid-year election carryover + HSA payroll deductions. Can Benefits + Payroll confirm what will change?

nina (Benefits): Quick summary: Fidelity will import participant elections and YTD balances, but some items need manual review (loans, after-tax Roth balances, and pending auto-escalation flags). HSA/FSA payroll elections are separate; those will be configured in payroll system (Gusto) and should continue uninterrupted, but we need to reconcile pre-tax deduction codes.

omar (Payroll): Thanks. From payroll side: we push deductions to vendor using specific deduction codes. During the switchover payroll needs a mapping table. If Fidelity accepts the import, elections should carry. However auto-escalation flags are vendor-specific: if Principal had `escalation_active`, we must make sure Fidelity receives that attribute or employees will see default behavior.

jess (IC): Will this affect my year-to-date 401(k) contributions for things like vesting or matching? Also worried about my HSA pre-tax contributions stopping for a pay period.

nina (Benefits): YTD deferrals and balances are part of the transfer; your match eligibility is unchanged. Match is based on contributions posted by payroll; if a pay period fails to send the deduction (mapping mismatch), that pay period could be missed for employer match. We'll do dry-run payroll tests before cutover.

saurabh (People Ops): Action item: set up a test payroll run and a short all-hands FAQ. @omar can you coordinate a test run with Fidelity this week? Also want a short employee note explaining how to check balances post-migration and who to contact if contributions look wrong.

omar (Payroll): On it. Opening internal ticket: PAY-2026-78  mapping + dry-run with Fidelity. I'll schedule a payroll test on 2026-07-01 payroll cycle and capture the export. If anyone has a specific case (loans, Roth conversions, mid-year rollovers), DM me.

benefits-bot: Ticket created: PAY-2026-78. Expected completion: 2026-07-05.

nina (Benefits): Also note: Principal's auto-escalation is set at plan-level and we had a participant-level `escalation_suspended` flag for a few folks on leave. We will export that flag to Fidelity; if Fidelity doesn't support the same field, we'll manually maintain those suspensions until the next plan cycle. We'll include that in the FAQ.

jess (IC): Where will I see the new account at Fidelity? Will I need to re-enroll or sign anything?

nina (Benefits): You won't need to re-enroll. Fidelity will send a welcome packet/email with account access info. For any required e-sign forms (loan transfers etc.) you'll get direct instructions. Most employees just log in and verify balances.

saurabh (People Ops): Draft employee note (short):

"We are moving retirement plans from Principal to Fidelity on 2026-07-15. Your current elections and year-to-date balances will transfer automatically. Please log into Fidelity after 7/15 to verify your balances and elections. If you notice missing contributions or loan details, contact payroll@redwood.com with subject line 'PAY-2026-78'. HSA/FSA payroll deductions should continue; contact benefits@redwood.com if deductions stop."

nina (Benefits): I'll add FAQ bullets: how to verify match, what to do if auto-escalation was suspended, loans & Roth balances, and expected timeline for emails from Fidelity. Also provide the internal link to migration FAQ (internal): https://intranet.redwood/benefits/migration-2026 (internal).

omar (Payroll): Test run status: export generated and ingested by Fidelity sandbox. Found two deduction code mismatches for HSA (codes 34 vs 340) which would have caused a pause. Fix pushed to payroll config. Re-run scheduled for 2026-07-03.

benefits-bot: PAY-2026-78 updated: HSA mapping fix applied, second test scheduled.

jess (IC): Great catch  thanks for proactively testing. Anything employees should do now?

saurabh (People Ops): For employees: 1) No action needed now. 2) Look for an email from Fidelity after 7/15 to set a password. 3) If you are on leave or have a suspended auto-escalation, email benefits@redwood.com so we can confirm the flag transferred. We'll post the final FAQ in #benefits-updates tomorrow.

nina (Benefits): One more note on taxes: W-2 reporting stays the same; the vendor migration doesn't change tax treatment. Any mid-year corrections will be handled via payroll adjustments if needed.

omar (Payroll): Closing note: tracker updated, I'll post a short post-mortem in #people-ops after cutover. Ticket PAY-2026-78 remains open until we confirm production payrolls on 2026-07-15.

saurabh (People Ops): Thanks everyone. I'll finalize the employee note and send the calendar invite for the FAQ drop-in on 2026-07-16.
